content:
Apple has confirmed that it will hold a special product launch event titled "Welcome Home" next Tuesday (October 13), but it has yet to announce whether a keynote video will be released at the same time. Here is what we know so far.

Apple has not confirmed a "Welcome Home" keynote, but Mark Gurman says there will be an "online video presentation."

Apple has been reinventing its traditional product launch approach throughout the year. The MacBook Neo released in March was the first example—following the rollout of several other new products through press releases over consecutive days, it then made its debut as an in-person "hands-on" event for journalists.

It now appears that Apple's "Welcome Home" launch on October 13 will also break new ground in a similar fashion.

Unlike traditional events, Apple has not yet added "Welcome Home" to its Apple Events webpage. There are also no signs of any livestream on YouTube or the Apple TV app.

These circumstances could change in the days leading up to the event, but as things stand, they suggest that there will not be a keynote video on October 13.

However, Mark Gurman has pointed to a video presentation in a Bloomberg report. In an article discussing another Apple event set for October 27, Gurman wrote:

According to Gurman—who had previously accurately reported the October 13 date and that the event would focus on Home products—Apple will hold an "online video presentation" next week.

The media will attend an "Apple Experience" event in New York, beginning at 9 a.m. local time that day. So if a launch video is released on the day, it will most likely go live at that time, considerably earlier than the usual airing time for a keynote.

We expect at least three new products to debut on Tuesday; you can find the details here.

Do you think Apple will release a keynote video for "Welcome Home"? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
